texts.preamble: Kumari Akshatha S vs The Branch Manager on 29 February, 2020 Before Motor Vehicles Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru City. Scch14 Dated this the 29Th Day Of February 2020 Present: Sri.SREEPADA.N., B.Com.,LL.M., Member, Mact, Xvi Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru.
texts.facts: SCCH14 3 MVC No.726/2019 2. Brief averments of the petition are as under: As per the case of the petitioner that, she is being minor and represented by her natural guardian father. That, on 22.01.2019 at about 3.30 p.m., when the petitioner was riding the Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA05HY7442 on Ganakal main road, carefully and cautiously, observing all the traffic rules and regulations, when she reached near Pavani Famiy restaurant, Ganakal main road, Kengeri, Bengaluru at that time the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA41MB9194 came in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, neglecting all the traffic rules and regulations, without blowing horn or giving any signal, came mindlessly and recklessly lost control of his car and dashed against minor petitioner's scooter. As a result of which, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body. It is further submitted that, immediately after the accident petitioner was shifted to BGS Global Hospital as an inpatient. Accordingly, petitioner has has spent huge amount towards medicine, conveyance, nourishment food, attendant charges and other incidental charges etc., It is further submitted that, at the time of the accident petitioner was student, due to the injuries sustained in the SCCH14 4 MVC No.726/2019 said accident the petitioner was on rest even to this day due to the injuries sustained in the accident and in future also the petitioner is unable to participate in curricular activities in the school and college and she is brilliant student in the school. It is further submitted that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent act of the Kumari Akshatha S vs The Branch Manager on 29 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101728172/ 2 driver of the offending car. It is further submitted that, the Kengeri Traffic police have registered the case in Crime No.0012/2019 against the driver of offending car for the offences punishable under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC. The respondents No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being owner of the vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation. Hence, the petitioner prayed for awarding compensation with interest and cost. 3. In response to the notice, the respondent No.2 is absent and placed exparte and respondent No.1 is appeared before the Tribunal through its counsel and filed its written statement. The petitioner's father being natural guardian examined himself as PW.1, examined one Dr.Raju K.P., Senior Consultant, Orthopedic Surgeon at BGS Hospital, Bengaluru as PW.2 and in all got marked Ex.P.1 to 14 documents. On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has examined its Senior Executive Officer as RW.1 but not marked any documents. In this case, the petitioner has filed this petition seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident that occurred on 22.01.2019 due to actionable negligence on the part of driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA41MB9194, when the minor petitioner was riding Honda Activa Scooter on Ganakal main road, near Pavani Restaurant, Kengeri, Bengaluru, at that time the driver of offending Car bearing Reg.No.KA41MB9194 came in a high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's scooter etc. Further the petitioner examined one Dr.Raju K.P, Senior Consultant, Orthopedic Surgeon, at BGS Hospital, Bengaluru as PW.2 and in all got marked Ex.P.1 to 14 documents. 11. Kumari Akshatha S vs The Branch Manager on 29 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101728172/ 5 Further stated that, he can produce the documents to show that he has not obtained any insurance amount from Bajaj Insurance Company. 13. Besides on perusal of Ex.P.1 FIR with complaint reveals that, police constable has given requisition with regard to the accident on the date of the accident itself stating that, on 22.01.2019 at about 3.45 p.m., he received information that accident had occurred at Ganakallu main SCCH14 12 MVC No.726/2019 road then he went to the said place and after inquiry he found that offending Car bearing Reg.No.KA41MB9194 came in a nice road in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against to the petitioner's scooter which was coming from Srinivasa Colony and then dashed two pedestrians who are coming by the side of the road and petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the said accident, as such, she got admitted to BGS hospital etc., Further on perusal of Ex.P.2 spot mahazar with sketch reveals that, the accident had occurred at junction and at the time of the accident the petitioner came from BSK 6th Stage, 11th block towards main road and at that time the offending car came from nice road towards Aditya Bakery and when the petitioner entered into circle about to take turn to the left side towards Aditya Bakery the offending car dashed against the petitioner's scooter.
texts.arguments: Further contended that, the respondents No.1 has denied the case of the petitioner as false and contended that the petition is not at all maintainable either in law or SCCH14 5 MVC No.726/2019 on facts. Further contended that, this respondents has denied the age avocation and income of the deceased. Further contended that, the compensation and interest as claimed by the petitioners are exorbitant and excessive. Further denied all the allegations found in the petition other than those that are specifically admitted that, this respondent has issued a private car policy package policy bearing No.OG19 1701182500001866 in favour of 2 nd respondent in respect of New Maruthi Baleno Car having Engine & Chassis No.4453049 & MA3EWB22SJH552718 and is is valid from 03.11.2018 to 2.11.2019 and their liability, if any is strictly in terms and conditions. Further contended that, respondent No.2 willfully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving license to drive the same as on the date of the accident. In fact the alleged accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding the motorcycle by the petitioner without possessing the driving license to ride the motorcycle and not having insurance to use that vehicle on the public road and not wearing safety headgear. Thus the petitioner being guilt of violation of motorcycle rules and regulations, she is not entitled for any compensation by the SCCH14 6 MVC No.726/2019 hands of this court. Further contended that, compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant and it has no rationale. The petitioner is not entitled to claim any compensation much less claimed Rs.9,00,000/ with interest at 9% p.a., Hence, on other grounds, the respondent No.1 has prayed for dismissal of the claim petition with costs. 6. The learned counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the decisions reported in; 1. 2018 ACJ 2465, High Court of Punjab and Haryana, Palo Vs Rajesh Sahni and another. 2. 2018 ACJ 2656, High Court of Bombay, Chandrakanth Vs. Majlasbai and other. According to Ex.P.3 IMV report it is clear that, head light assembly, pannel, handle bar, front right side shape, rear right side shape of the petitioner's scooter has been damaged and front wind screen glass, right side portion of bumper, front right side, front right side head light assembled of offending car has been damaged and according to IMV inspector the accident was not taken place due to any mechanical defects of both vehicles and brake system of both vehicle were in order. Admittedly, the damages are caused to both vehicles reveals that, both petitioner and the driver of the offending vehicle were in high speed at the time of the accident. So, due to fault of the both of them the accident had occurred. Even on perusal of Ex.P.4 - wound certificate reveals that, petitioner had sustained injuries in the said accident. SCCH14 14 MVC No.726/2019 It is the specific contention of the petitioner's counsel is that, even though the petitioner was minor at the time of the accident and not holding driving license no contributing negligence filed on her in the accidednt when the charge sheet has been filed against the driver of the offending car. In this regard he has relied upon the decision reported in 2018 ACJ Kumari Akshatha S vs The Branch Manager on 29 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101728172/ 6 2465 (High Court of Punjab and Haryana). However he himself has relied upon another decision which is reported in 2019 ACJ 1931 Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru wherein it is held that; Negligence - contributory negligence - minor - driving license - absence of - lorry driven at fast speed dashed against a motorcycle resulting in death of motorcyclist - tribunal found that since deceased was a minor who was not holding a driving license he contributed to the accident - tribunal held that lorry driver was negligent to the extent of 75% and deceased contributed to the accident to the extent of 25% tribuna's finding upheld. Similarly in the case on hand also, petitioner was minor at the time of the accident and not holding driving license and in the junction the accident had occurred due to minor negligence on the part of the petitioner and as well as major negligence on the part of the driver of offending car. Hon'ble Supreme Court has held ruling reported in ILR 2013 KAR 4891 (Master Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager) as under: (a) Though it is difficult to have an accurate assessment of compensation in the case of children suffering disability on account of a motor vehicle accident, having regard to the relevant factors, precedents and the approach of various High Courts, that the appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment attendant, etc., should be, if the disability is above 10% and up 30% to the SCCH14 21 MVC No.726/2019 whole body, Rs.3 lakhs; upto 60% Rs.4 lakhs; upto 90%, Rs.5 lakhs and above 90%, it should be 6 lakhs,.
